rationale: This task is suitable for AsynCodeBench because it has three natural but dependent responsibilities: the first-class Return IR schema and visitor contract, the TVMScript construction and rendering surface, and legality/lowering plus C and LLVM target emission. The Script owner consumes the Return node, value field, FFI constructor, and visitor semantics produced by the IR-core owner; the backend owner then consumes the Script-produced Return representation. Public role-ablation evidence progresses from base 0/8 to core 3/8, core plus Script 5/8, and complete integration 8/8, while the selected regression suite reports 782 passes and three expected failures. In private asynchronous work, the Script layer may retain the retired legacy-return intrinsic or the backend may retire that contract before the Script migration, producing round-trip, legality, build, or malformed-control-flow failures. The roles can make local progress, but both directed contracts require coordinated integration, so partially_parallelizable is the appropriate label.
